newsitem.title: USA: Nationwide sees claims from Fran topping $200 mln.
newsitem.headline: Nationwide sees claims from Fran topping $200 mln.

text.p: Nationwide Insurance Enterprise on Wednesday said its claims cost projection for Hurricane Fran has risen to between $195 and $205 million.
The number of claims has topped 62,500 so far, versus earlier projections of 50,000 claims and $150 million in cost.
If the new estimate were reached, the claims cost would surpass the company's record payout of $179 million for Hurricane Hugo, which smashed into South Carolina in 1989.
Hurricane Fran struck North Carolina Sept. 5 and caused widespread damage.

"We've paid more than $156 million to close to 59,200 claims from Hurricane Fran, and we have 3,400 claims pending," said Paul Thompson, Nationwide vice president of property-casualty claims. "Meanwhile, we've been averaging 200 new claims daily."
Meanwhile, Thompson said that claims from Hurricane Josephine, which stuck the U.S. mainland on Oct. 7, have been "relatively light, but widespread." Ten states were affected.
